notes: encoding::base32: one Engine type with Go's behaviour (CR/LF skipped, Go's CorruptInputError offsets and partial output on error via decode_into), differential-checked by tools/base32_check.py. Decoding is a port of Go's quantum state machine. Engine::new and with_padding return Result where Go panics; Engine::new takes a 32-byte array, so a wrong alphabet length cannot be expressed. with_padding takes Option<u8>, so padding above 0xff, which Go rejects, cannot be expressed. encode returns a String (U+FFFD for a non-UTF-8 byte of a custom alphabet); encode_to_vec returns the raw bytes. Decoder is a port of Go's stream decoder (1024-byte buffer, per-read newline filtering), so data after padding is an error only when it arrives in a later chunk and corrupt offsets are chunk-relative, as Go; where Go returns data with an error, Decoder returns the data and then the error on the next read. The differential also compares chunked-read schedules (caller buffer size and source bytes per read) record by record

CorruptInputError.Error.note: Display gives Go's 'illegal base32 data at input byte N'

Encoding.AppendDecode.note: bytes decoded before a corrupt byte stay in the Vec

Encoding.Decode.note: appends to a Vec instead of filling a sized slice; bytes before a corrupt byte are kept, as in Go

Encoding.Encode.note: appends to a Vec instead of filling a sized slice

Encoding.EncodeToString.note: encode_to_vec returns raw bytes when a custom alphabet or padding is not ASCII

Encoding.WithPadding.note: Takes Option<u8> (None is NoPadding) and returns an error where Go panics on an invalid padding byte.

NewDecoder.note: io::Read adapter; Go's (n, err) pair is returned as data first, then the error

NewEncoder.note: io::Write adapter; Go's Close is Encoder::finish, which flushes the final quantum and returns the inner writer

NewEncoding.note: Returns Result<Self, AlphabetError> (an error where Go panics on an invalid alphabet).
